text_fidelity_a:
Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display I so desperately want this to be great that apparently I ordered one 2 years ago and blocked it out of my memory and just received another one. Here are the issues:

1) If you have a good ergonomic keyboard (I have Microsoft 4000), then the keys on this are no better.

2) You will never have enough keys on there. Where is Escape? Number Keys? Large space bar? WSAD keys? Sure you can assign most of them but it just won't work well enough.

3) If you are thinking about assigning the the top row to numbers, it doesn't work well. It was designed for the middle top key to be your W in your WSAD keys (Those 4 have a nice curved depression for you to feel them here).

4) Reassigning WSAD to a lower set of keys will make your fingers cramped and start aching in no time.

5) I use Steam, adding Steam games to this is a HUGE pain the... um, fingers. First, I see no documentation about it. Second this thing wants to know exactly where the games are. That's no easy task when you have a few hundred steam games, the icon on your desktop won't work.

6) It doesn't autodetect what's running on my Windows 8 64bit machine. I even ran it as administrator.

7) It's not natural. You constantly want your fingers go where they have for years if you are a veteran to keyboard usage.

8) You spend more time wondering and looking down which key you assigned what to, where your hand is on the keys, where you assigned 3, 4, or other numbers to than you should.

9) In the end, I keep going back to my keyboard.

Hopefully I'll remember that this is not as good as I imagine and want it to be and stop ordering it every couple of years.
text_fidelity_b: Logitech G13 Programmable Gameboard with LCD Display

Ergear Dual Monitor Stand for 13 to 32 inch, Heavy Duty Fully Adjustable, Mount Fits up to 17.6 lbs per Arm, EGCM1 Ok...so I just finished mounting my monitors on these arms. It looks great and feels sturdy. But one important thing to note is that it takes a LOT of strength to get the nuts tight enough to hold the monitor’s position, especially in regards to up-and-down tilt. I kept tightening...and tightening...and tightening...until I thought my thumb was going to break off. I finally got them tight enough to stop drooping and hold the position. The same is true for the main arm which holds up the crossbar. I’m still a little leery that it’s going to start slipping after a while, but for now, I think it’s probably secure. I will tighten up the bolts again in a few days just to be sure. It would be nice if they included some time of tool that was easier to grip rather than an Allen wrench, especially when that much tightening is needed.

I will say that the clamp and main post are heavy duty and feel very sturdy. Also, the arms are easy to move and reposition side to side and back and forth. I also like that I was able to mount the monitors without a second person, due to the assisting bolts where you can “hang” the monitor on the bracket until you get everything screwed tight (like a ceiling fan).

Overall 4 stars due to my hands and arms are going to be sore tomorrow due to all the required tightening.
text_fidelity_b: Ergear Dual Monitor Stand for 13 to 32 inch, Heavy Duty Fully Adjustable, Mount Fits up to 17.6 lbs per Arm, EGCM1

Highly, highly recommend. Probably my favorite out of all the ones I've tried.. and I've tried about 7 just this past year.
Splurge and get them, you will not regret it.

text_fidelity_a:
Fujifilm FinePix J40 12.2 MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Zoom and 3-Inch LCD (Includes 2 GB SD Memory Card) The camera is $[..]for gosh sakes! It's an amazing little piece of technology. The 3X optics and 12.2MP CMOS camera are well matched in the optical train to provide a great image for casual photos adequate for most users. It's the simplest start-up I've ever seen. The viewer LCD provides a maximum size to the package. `The manual' is 7 steps of which 4 include inserting memory, battery, charging battery and turning it on. It's `point and shoot' in the extreme.

I work in the domain of optics & imaging design. My wife has a 5 year old Fuji camera of this same genre that I've gone to some lengths to compare with Nikon and Canon in this low cost market. Without getting technical ... for the old Fuji, there are no user discernable image quality differences. The Fuji optics were superior (i.e. best objective lens light capture and transfer). Take your pick between the 3 on the backend image processing system/PC interface.

My wife has carried the 5 year old Fuji in her purse every day ... that's a technically demanding reliability challenge. Fuji can be relied on to deliver the best value for money in an image capture platform if you're designing a million dollar platform or this $69 platform. You're not paying the premium for the huge advertisement budget of Nikon and Canon when you buy Fuji. I think you just get a better camera.

I can't speak to this unit's reliability for now. A 3x optical train with autofocus, f-stop, etc mechanisms and micro motors are robust to a point. They will all fail, even the highest dollar product, if exposed to the wrong environment (g-shock, sand, salt spray, thermal shock, etc).

One reviewer mentioned software loading problems. I had absolutely no problems on a Windows 7, 64bit OS.

You can't go wrong with this device. It's an excellent camera for you or the kids or the g-kids for Xmas.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm FinePix J40 12.2 MP Digital Camera with 3x Optical Zoom and 3-Inch LCD (Includes 2 GB SD Memory Card)

Echo Auto (1st gen) - Hands-free Alexa in your car with your phone I love my echo Auto! I'm disabled, have an old car, without Bluetooth or an auxiliary port. So, I use a Bluetooth transmitter to hook up my echo Auto, and month after month it has gotten better and better. Yes, there were plenty of glitches in the beginning, but every time I left feedback, the problems I had seemed to be fixed the next time I drove- which is only about once a week.
I live away from the city, I have a Samsung Note 8 and sometimes my signal that's not very great, so in a spot or two, the signal gets lost, then picks right back up very quickly. Navigation works great, with my phone suctioned to the side window showing Google Maps as I drive.
But, the greatest thing for me, is being able to listen to music from my playlists. I love all different kinds of music, and there's no radio station that can accommodate that. But, having Pandora and Amazon music playlists at the ready, I'm singing along with every song! Another Plus, it has made my stereo sound so much better!! The music is loud and clear, and I like the bass turned up just a tad... 😉🎶🎵🎶
Being a new product, I expected, and still expect a few glitches here and there. But I can say, I'm really glad I have this little device in my car along for the ride. It's great for someone who is disabled, and I can only imagine that it will keep getting better.

ClearStream Micron-R Indoor HDTV Antenna with Reflector - 35 Mile Range I have a roof-top antenna that worked well for analog stations but, when I converted to digital, I went from receiving 8 stations to just 1. After trying a few other antennas, I came across the ClearStream 4. I'm able to pull in 20+ digital stations perfectly, and 4 more so-so. Several analog stations come in as well, but the picture is not nearly as good as the digitial stations.

The antenna is well-made, but is a bit of a pain to assemble - lots of pieces to screw together. It only takes about 10 minutes, but you'll probably need to utter a few choice words since it's hard to get the screws to line up properly. The directions are pretty spotty, but give you the essential information. The brackets are heavy-duty, and everything is either aluminum or plastic, so it should hold up well to the elements if I put it outside. Right now, it is in my attic, and may stay there since it pulls in all the stations I want to watch. It does not come with a cable.

It's pretty compact given its performance, and much more compact that the DB8 (another Antenna Direct model with about the same specifications). Very happy with the performance. Also have a DB2 -- see my comments on that review that compare it to this antenna in terms of performance.
text_fidelity_b: ClearStream Micron-R Indoor HDTV Antenna with Reflector - 35 Mile Range

text_fidelity_a: Telescopes for Adults Kids Beginners, 400/70 Astronomical AZ Telescope with The Sturdy Stainless Tripod, Professional Refractor Telescope for Planetary and Terrestrial Landscape Observation. This was my first telescope.  I have read a lot about telescopes and plan on buying a much more expensive one but then I read that you can take a scope like this and upgrade the eye piece and the finder scope and have something very usable for a basic telescope.  It is below zero here so rather than go outside I did all my reviewing inside looking out my window at the mountain.  The listing provides a great overview of what you get with the scope so I won't detail it here.  I will say that it does comes with everything you need to get ab great intro into having a telescope of this type.  The trip is very shaky  and when you look out at such a great distance any movement of the tripod makes focusing difficult. Using a remote for your camera or phone would work best.  It comes with a phone adapter so I attached an older phone to it and took a couple of nice shots of a portion of the top of the mountain.  Given I didn't have to do much I thought they turned out pretty good.  The focus needs improvement but I guess I wasn't expecting a lot from this lens.  The finder scope is used to first find the object you want to see in the telescope.  It worked fine.  Then you go to the telescope lens and the object should be there and all you need to do is focus, which I did.  Because the tripod is shaky it is hard to get a good focus as just touching the eye piece cause it to shake.  This is a very inexpensive tripod and most good scopes would require a tripod 3 times the cost of this entire product.  For this price you are getting an intro to using a telescope.  With some experience with this I should be able to get better at focusing.  I took these mountain pix with the 25mm eye piece.  It comes with a nice carrying case for the scope and tripod.  There is also a nice small case for the lenses.  The instructions and well done with a nice bird watching book included also.  I will enjoy taking this with me when I go camping where maybe I will see some birds.  I highly recommend this scope as a good start for getting into this hobby.
text_fidelity_b: Telescopes for Adults Kids Beginners, 400/70 Astronomical AZ Telescope with The Sturdy Stainless Tripod, Professional Refractor Telescope for Planetary and Terrestrial Landscape Observation.

text_fidelity_a:
OP/TECH USA Soft Pouch Digital D-Pro (Black) I bought this cover and the Zing Pro Zoom cover. I like the Op Tech D Pro Zoom better.
Pros:
It was easier to get on and off my camera then the Zing.
It fits my camera and accessories nicely.
Seems well made. I have many other Op Tech products that I purchased and they have all held up nicely.
Cons:
To securely close the cover, there is a flap that has 2 snaps. You wrap the cover around the back of the camera, and snap the flap closed with the 2 snaps. I'm not a fan of snaps. These were easy to snap closed, but Velcro would have been much easier.
There is a strap attached to the inside of the cover. It came with 2 ways of attaching the cover to your camera so you don't lose the cover:
1. a piece of leather that attaches to the camera by screwing it into the tripod mount. This piece attaches to the strap with a snap. I could see either end of the leather coming apart - the side with screw could detach or the snap could release.
2. A ring that can go around the lens. This ring attaches to the strap with a snap. I don't like having things attached to my lens and the snap could release.
I came up with my own method of securing the cover to my camera. The bottom of my battery grip has a connection point for a strap. I had an extra set of Op Tech Uni Loop connectors (https://www.amazon.com/OP-TECH-USA-1301062-Uni-Loop/dp/B0010HA6A6/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1485137755&sr=8-1&keywords=optech+uni+loop).
I attached one end to the bottom of the battery grip. I attached the other connector to the strap by looping the strap thru the connector loop and snapping the two snaps on the strap together. Using the uni loop connectors, I clicked the two pieces together. I think the weakest point is where the snaps are attached. I'm going to sew a few stitches next to the strap as a precaution in case the snaps come undone. You can use any type of strap to secure the cover to the camera. I also attached a photo using an extra camera strap from one of my point and shoot cameras. If I used this method, I would still sew a few stitches next to the snap. I like the uni loop method. If the cover gets in the way, I can just disconnect the uni loop clips.
I'm happy with this cover even though I'm using a different method of attaching the cover to my camera. I dropped the rating to a 4 because of the use of the snaps.
text_fidelity_b: OP/TECH USA Soft Pouch Digital D-Pro (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Technics Premium in- Ear Monitors IEM, High-Fidelity Wired in-Ear Earbuds Earphones with Innovative 10mm Driver for Ultra-Low Distortion - EAH-TZ700, Black/Gold I work in live AV production, and usually keep a pair of Sony over-the-ear headphones in my gear bag for monitoring sound on location. Quality of the sound is important for concert and other live music gigs. But those big Sonys take up a lot of space, so I've been considering a good set of IEMs for a while now. In the past I haven't had good results from anything that wasn't a large over-the-ear set, and I have small ears that reject a lot of ear-bud style devices so I was excited to get a chance to try these out.

Ok, to be fair, I don't have any other IEMs to compare this to, but I'm BLOWN AWAY at how incredible they sound at such a miniscule size. I put on the smallest tips for my ears and they actually stay in relatively well, and create the passive noise cancellation I was expecting but without being uncomfortable to wear for an extended period of time. But the range of sound reproduced was something I have only experienced in larger studio headphones!
A perk of IEMs versus larger headphones on jobs like mine are that I can pull out one so I can hear the sound around me while monitoring with my other ear (great if working with an audio engineer who needs to communicate with me on the job), and it comes with a pretty nifty case to wrap it up and slide into my bag. The case makes it bigger than it needs to be, but honestly this is so much less space than my old headphones took up, and keeps the cord from getting tangled. I love it!
For personal use, they sound great even on consumer equipment, but they really shine on devices that can drive the additional range such as my old LG V20 with it's Quad DAC built in (one of the reasons I keep that old device around!).
The price tag is a little steep for me personally, but my Sony headphones retail somewhere around this (I had bought them used), and I KNOW there are pricier options out there, so it seems to fit right into the audiophile equipment range.
text_fidelity_b: Technics Premium in- Ear Monitors IEM, High-Fidelity Wired in-Ear Earbuds Earphones with Innovative 10mm Driver for Ultra-Low Distortion - EAH-TZ700, Black/Gold

It couldn't be simpler. I understand that a cell phone can be used to call 911, as well; however, it takes awhile for my cell phone to power up. It's not always easy to use. This device is simple and, hopefully, works as well as promised.

Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO V2 CPU Air Cooler with SickleFlow 120, PWM Fan, Direct Contact Technology, 4 Copper Heat Pipes for AMD Ryzen/Intel LGA1700/1200/1151, Silver/Black I have had this CPU fan now going on 5 months. I love this fan. I hadn't upgraded for nearly 10 years and decided on an AMD FM2 Black Edition 6300 6-core CPU with an MSI 970A-G43 Plus economy Micro Board and 16GB of Corsair Memory 4GBx4 in the 4 slots. I use my computer for gaming and all around use. I wanted a CPU cooler that would be quiet and still keep my cpu cool when I cranked it up for high-performance gaming. I found it with this AND it didn't break the bank. With the Turbo Clock OC setting it will idle down and bolt up to 4300mhz seamlessly while the fan moves from it's WHISPER silent 36c idle and general use, to it's 42c full bore o'clocked gaming use. The fan keeps it cool, and never does the fan become obtrusive or loud.

This fan is BIG. Don't even consider it if you have a micro or small mid-tower case. Your case must be generous in it's width to accommodate this cooler. Be sure to check the dimensions of your case with the unit. I have an older Antec 900 case it fit snugly into. I did have to remove the optional side window cooler intake fan I had installed with the prev board, cpu and cooler to allow it's fit. Also be sure your motherboard design placement of Memory slots is such that your Memory will clear it. My board's Corsair Vengence Memory JUST cleared it by a couple mm's laterally, and the top of the memory overtakes the bottom edge of cooler by about a quarter inch. If you are in the process of building your system a choice with low profile memory that doesn't have the tall heat spreaders would be a wise choice and safe bet if you are unsure about clearance with a board design that puts the memory slots very close to the CPU and cooler position. In the first photo attached I REVERSED the fan position to PULL the air thru on Left for best clearance instead of PUSHING the air through on the right if you just don't have the room, that flexibility is very handy. I wasn't satisfied with the cooling level and re-positioned the fan on right to PUSH it through later on and it sent the temps down a few more degrees. As you can see though in the second photo, it is much more snug.

Bottom line, a great cooler IF your case and build offers the room to fit it in. I would recommend it for those wanting great overclocking cooling performance and very quiet operation. I think most overclock enthusiasts would be well served to try this value priced solution before expensive and complicated water cooled solutions.
text_fidelity_b: Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO V2 CPU Air Cooler with SickleFlow 120, PWM Fan, Direct Contact Technology, 4 Copper Heat Pipes for AMD Ryzen/Intel LGA1700/1200/1151, Silver/Black

If you don’t watch any HDCP-protected content on your system I still highly recommend this adapter. Sadly though, if you do watch such content, introducing this adapter into the signal path (or even just plugging it into your MacBook, regardless of whether you're actually using any of its ports) will prevent you from doing so.

The main product picture currently being used shows a silver stand; the stand is actually black as shown in other product photos. I can’t really say if the design of the stand frees up more desk space or not since that’s never been a problem for me, but I do like that it’s a flat base. The viewing angle is adjustable but not the height of the monitor.

I also like the slim power cord! No huge brick adaptor for this monitor.

The main complaint I have with this monitor is how it bounces on my desk. I use a mechanical keyboard, and the monitor bobbles with every keystroke. I have a larger monitor that doesn’t have this problem, so I imagine it’s due to the small stand on the Dell.

Image quality seems to be pretty good. There’s not a ton of options on the monitor, but you can adjust contrast/brightness, and there are presets for “ComfortView” (blue light blocking), Movie, Game, Warm, Cool, and the ability to set a custom color.

When I use it with my laptop, I do my main work on the Dell screen instead of the Mac’s, which is the opposite of what I usually do. And not because of the increased screen size, but because I prefer the image quality.

text_fidelity_a:
MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP THINGS YOU'LL NEED THAT ARE NOT INCLUDED:
----------------------------------------------------------
1. Your own micro SD card, up to 2tb.
2. A power adapter that has a usb-c port. The Qubii will be plugged into this adapter.
3. A usb-c to usb-c cable. To connect from the Qubii to the usb-c port of your Android phone.
4. A usb-c to Apple lightning if you'll be using an iPhone.

SOME NOTEWORTHY INFO:
---------------------------------
* This is a good idea, now that Google Photos is no longer unlimited.
* It basically backs-up every folder that has an image. There doesn't seem to be a way to choose which folders you want it to back-up. I only need my main camera folder to get backed-up, but oh well, backing up too much is better than too little.
* Once you disconnect from power adapter, you can use the Qubii as OTG storage. You'll need to turn on OTG storage in your system settings. If you have a case on your phone, you'll probably never bother to use it as OTG because you'll need to remove the case.
* Every time you want to transfer files to your PC, NAS, etc., you'll need to remove the micro sd card if your pc doesn't have a usb-c port. My PC does not, so I use a usb to usb-c adapter. This eliminates the hassle of having to take out micro sd cards, dealing with card readers, etc.
* After you transfer everything safely to your pc, if you delete the files on the micro SD card to clear space, the Qubii still maintains its count. So even if these files are still on your phone, it will not re-download them again.

In conclusion, how accurate and precise this system is remains to be seen. So far, it has backed up everything I need it to. I know people complain of missing files, not everything getting backed-up, etc. Most of these complaints revolves around people using iPhones. But we'll see, time will tell. As of now, this is 5-Stars!
text_fidelity_b: MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP

text_fidelity_a:
TP-Link AC750 Wireless Wi-Fi Gigabit Router (Archer C2) I am not super "techie" like some of the other folks reviewing this router, just your average housewife who likes gadgets and tries not to drown in the constant wave of weekly tech improvements. As such, I wanted a new router to replace our two year old dual band Belkin with similar speed output, but only a single antenna. The Belkin had a number of dead spots despite using one of those extender things and I had had enough. Enter this TP-Link router.

I was wary of the installation after seeing some other reviews and the difficulties folks have been reporting. However, after reading the box and the instructions fully FIRST and then following the directions exactly, I had no problems. One thing I did notice immediately, is this router is meant to be used with a cable modem and that modem must be powered off before you connect it to this router. I used the website installation method and was up and going in a total of 20 minutes - that is from opening the box to having all our wireless stuff connected to the internet again. The website management page is very detailed and allows for a lot of customization of your network, honestly, more than I need or understand. But changing the router's password and setting our network name was simple and worked on the first try.

After three days of use I like it. The speed is decent and the dual antenna set up has improved the coverage problem we were having with the old Belkin router. I haven't experienced any slowdown or degradation of connectivity with multiple devices going at once thus far. A Fire Phone surfing the net, Fire tablet streaming music, laptop doing email, and a smart tv streaming video all at once in different rooms. So...a good router for every day family use in a pretty typical home.

*********** UPDATE FEBRUARY 2015 ***********
After 90 days this router is trouble free and really working like a champ. Our cable company upgraded our modem and increased our internet speeds recently, requiring a full shutdown and reconnect of my entire network. It was a snap and the router has had no problem with faster connection and the new modem. I relocated everything to the center of our house when everything was being swapped out and the router is now sending a five bar signal out to the back deck, which means I can sit out there with the dogs in nice weather to do email etc.

*****************UPDATE APRIL 2016 *************

I'm still using this router every single day for literally every single WiFi device in our house and it just does its job with zero drama every day. We now have two tablets, two smartphones, three DVR boxes on WiFi, two laptops, a printer, a Fire Stick for streaming movies, a smart tv connected the web now and then, and the Echo that's connected all the time. (yeah, I know...we watch a LOT of television in this house!)

Right this minute I am streaming music on the Echo, recording tv shows on two different DVR boxes, using my laptop to update this review, and uploading 42 photos from my phone to the cloud and pushing email to my tablet. Oh - and I am sitting outside on the patio enjoying the lovely spring day. This router is powerful and I have no dead spots inside or out in the backyard.
text_fidelity_b: TP-Link AC750 Wireless Wi-Fi Gigabit Router (Archer C2)

I was surprised at how heavy duty this cable actually was. It's almost too heavy. I've found it hard to flex and keep in place and while my portable hard drives are weighty enough to stay in place I could see this cable dragging a lighter phone or other device off a desk.

I had no problems with fit or connections and while it may be my imagination (I've run my backups hundreds of times over the last couple years so I know how long it normally takes) it seems like data transfer might be just a bit faster with this cable than with the ones Seagate sent out with their drives.

This is a well made, possibly too heavy for light devices, cable from AmazonBasics. I have used AmazonBasics cables for quite a while now and never had a problem with any of them.

Midland 50 Channel Waterproof GMRS Two-Way Radio - Long Range Walkie Talkie with 142 Privacy Codes, SOS Siren, and NOAA Weather Alerts and Weather Scan (Black/Silver, Pair Pack) I am always amazed at what people can come up to complain about. (But I'll get to that in a second.)

I own about a dozen radios that cost around $400 each. They are incredibly high quality and obviously very expensive too. But they are not the kind of radios you would camp or backpack with. They are too heavy and large for that application.

So, I did my research and bought these Midland radios. AND THEY ARE GREAT!! They have a clear and strong signal under reasonable conditions for ANY radio. Some of these reviews that whine about range clearly don't understand how radios work. They are not cell phones using giant towers that carry your signal across the nation. Radios--whether they are $400 each or $40 each, cannot overcome solid obstacles like houses and trees and mountains indefinitely. I was impressed at how well these did under less than ideal conditions.

Ignore these reviewers that have unattainable standards and get these radios.

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White I ordered a three pack because I wanted one for my music room, living room and one for my girlfriend. Set up was super simple for the basics - connecting to a bluetooth speaker, your calendar (I use google's calendar), and a music source. For the latter I use Pandora and that, too, was simple.

The subtracted star is because while I own a few thousand dollars worth of MP3 albums that I purchased from Amazon, I cannot access them. Apparently you can only stream music from Amazon's cloud if you have Prime, and even then I am not sure that you can access any of your own music that resides in their cloud. To me that is a fail, and an indication that the business and requirements analysts who assisted in the development of this device do not fully understand customer requirements at a very basic level. Another nit is the iHeart Radio music source that is plain confusing to use.

Some other areas where this would be a LOT more useful is to have the ability to set up more than one route for traffic (currently I can only identify a single route, home-to-work or back, whereas I am frequently traveling from one place to the other and traffic conditions for those trips would be very helpful. The same for the calendar: you can get all events for a single day, but not for a week, or weekend so you still have to fire up a calendar app on your phone, tablet or computer if you want to get a sense of how busy you will be over a period longer than a day.

Still, for fifty bucks each - plus the discount for purchasing a three pack - this is a decent device that has proven to be surprisingly useful in my home. My girlfriend instantly took to hers too. In the week or so that I have been using it I find that I am growing increasingly dependent on mine for streaming music from Pandora, looking up quick information while I am reading or watching a documentary, and letting me know what is on my calendar for a specific day.

I have one of mine connected via bluetooth to a [[ASIN:B019PGACR0 LD Systems MAUI 5 Channel PA System]], and my girlfriend has hers connected to a [[ASIN:B00W8O6MJO Creative Sound Blaster Roar 2 Portable NFC Bluetooth Speaker]], both of which greatly out perform the larger Echo. However I also use my other Dot with just its integrated speaker and it is more than adequate, even for streaming music since I have it on an end table.

Overall, for the current fifty bucks this is a bargain (warts notwithstanding), and while I purchased mine more out of curiosity all three have proven to be useful and practical.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

This Intel Core i3-based laptop is astonishingly, agonizingly slow. I bought this to replace a 7 year-old MacBook Pro that had served well, but didn't have the horsepower to run the latest version of OS X. This Acer is only marginally faster than the MacBook, and feels slower in may respects. It's glacially sluggish to start-up or restart, and Excel and Word crawl along at speeds reminiscent of 1980s era PCs. Browser speeds - Chrome, IE, and the execrable Edge - all range from stagnant to plodding.

Other, more minor, negatives: the track pad might as well be 50 shades of gray, because it requires an extremely firm touch. The PC case is some form of black plastic that shows every fingerprint and smudge, all of which are impossible to remove.

I'm hoping for a day-after-Thanksgiving miracle deal to replace this cinder block of a PC.

Update 08.16.2017: Acer contacted me after this review was posted (big plus), and opened a case. They called me less than 24 hours after the case was opened (another big plus), but they had my laptop registered to someone else and I had to call them back when I had the laptop in front of me. The person I spoke with had me shutdown the laptop, and use a utility to reset system configurations to the default. When I restarted the computer, the performance had not improved. The support person commented that the laptop only has 4 GB of memory, which apparently makes it unsuited to running Excel. Acer sold the computer with this configuration, and no mention of not being able to run the MS Office suite (or open more than one tab on a browser). He then suggested wiping the computer and resetting it to the original state. I'm not willing to invest any more time in this laptop. Thanks to Acer for contacting me, but this one-star review stands. No more Acer products for me.

Netgear Unite AC770S | Mobile Wifi Hotspot 4G LTE | Up to 300Mbps Download Speed | Connect Up to 10 Devices | Create A WLAN Anywhere | 2 MIMO TS-9 external antenna connectors | GSM Unlocked - Black I'll update if there's a problem once I receive my FREE SIM card with FREE Express Mail from AT&T. The unit comes charged, and everything worked perfectly, connected to my laptop, WiFi name & password printed on sticker. Very, very nice, compact, well-designed device. Easy connection, easy info once I learned to use the built-in electronic screen and "Info". The "ICCID" number is the SIM number, it's under "Info" with the IMEA number in the electronic screen (AT&T will need both numbers for activation). The IMEA is also listed beneath battery. Slide two little metal sliders on side to remove back cover to remove battery. But you don't have to, it's in the electronic screen "Info" :)

Persons much more mechanically inclined than I will see that the door to the SIM card is on the side edge, not in the back or under the battery. I would have ruined the device trying to dig out the back compartment if my husband hadn't stopped me. He needed tweezers to get out the SIM card regardless.

This is a great, mobile, easy HotSpot device that works just like any Wi-Fi on any device with a great connection. Mobile supposedly for 10 hours, less than hour recharge.

There's only one caveat: AT&T will tell you the pre-installed SIM card it comes with, sealed in new packaging, is INVALID. AT&T will give you a good one for FREE. You simply have to replace it, or if you're like me, get someone that can. :) That simple, and you're ready for set-up. *NOTE*: Both the pre-installed SIM card *AND* the SIM card being sold by a separate seller on Amazon that is suggested as being a good companion purchase with this device are INVALID. This according to AT&T themselves. They will send you a new, free one you can use; tell them what device you have and setup a data plan.

All you need then is to add a Data plan. This device, according to AT&T, *only* works with a postpaid plan ($50.00/month for 5 G's minimum), however there's no contract. There is a credit check. It will not work with prepaid, it will not work with a lesser plan, no matter what the packaging or Amazon description says. I just spent like 20 minutes on the phone with a very helpful, patient, and knowledgeable AT&T customer service representative who also consulted another department for verification.

The one exception is if you already have an AT&T cellphone plan (I do), you can "share" your data package you already have for only $20/month. So that's what I did. It still is postpaid, and there still is no contract on that part of the plan with your new HotSpot device. You'll be given a new number that's only for the HotSpot without a cellphone (Voice) plan component.

I'm really glad I bought this great device, I was a little apprehensive because I'm not techie and I've never tried a mobile HotSpot device before. To make it simple, get AT&T to install (instore) or send you a new SIM card that they say works with this device, and then you can set up the device (supposedly) online with ease. You have to add a data plan for it. I'll update if there's a problem, but the connection to my laptop worked seamlessly and looking through the device hardware and software on the electronic screen, it's designed beautifully and is a definite winner! :) :)

ps. Oh!, and it DOES receive 4G out of the box! :) Shows right in the screen corner like a Cellphone would with the bars.

I really wanted just a plain old back up, but having an Electronics Engineering degree, I had to stay current. I can't really complain at this point, because I am backing up an 11 year old computer that is slowing to a crawl anyhow. It did not take long to set this drive up on my network. All of my devices immediately found it on the network and play music from the MBL. I had my Kindle HD out in the yard, playing music right off of MBL, while I do my gardening (downloaded the free app for Kindle). It was cool. I feel it will probably be short lived. Last year I bought a cheap WiFi receiver and it was so fast, this year it is so slow. I don't have high expectations from WiFi, and this drive only has the capability to plug into the network. It does not have USB connectivity at all. I do often times want a quick and easy way to transfer files to my new computer, while I do other things. The price was not too bad, but for that money I hope to be able to recover my data even after the WiFi dies. A good back up drive from WD usually last for years. That is what customers are accustomed to anyhow. I will probably update this review in one year. I did password protect my drive before the first file ever got added. I did update the firmware also. So far it is a nice thing to have.
My update on this drive is that it gets better as I use it. I don't know why that new things on my network start out slow and speed up as they are used, but it is working well.

Anker Soundcore Bluetooth Speaker with 24-Hour Playtime, 66-Feet Bluetooth Range & Built-in Mic, Dual-Driver Portable Wireless Speaker with Low Harmonic Distortion and Superior Sound - Blue I own the A3143 Premium Stereo Bluetooth speaker (2x10W=20W) which sounds great, but it doesn't have a microphone or the longer battery life of this lower-cost A3102 SoundCore speaker (2x3W=6W). The features and sound characteristics are different, but which is the better choice depends on personal preference. To me based on sound quality alone, the A3143 wins hands down. The bass is stronger (more power is required to drive the lower frequencies than the higher frequencies), but I also find overall frequency response to be more balanced and accurate for instruments and vocals. For either speaker, I'd recommend using an EQ app to set the frequency response and spatial effects to your preference (I use Bass EQ from Coocent). Interestingly, the maximum volume level for both the A3143 and this A3102 SoundCore are about the same.

The A3102 has a brighter sound overall. The A3102 is good as a general purpose speaker, and it is excellent to use with a cell phone. The A3102 microphone (which the A3143 doesn't have) and speaker quality for voice calling are crisp and clear. My dad who can't hear very well often could not understand me on my cell phone handset or its speakerphone, but had no problem when I used the A3102.

So for long battery life, good overall music speaker, and particularly for use as a microphone/speakerphone for voice calls, A3102 is a good choice. For best music reproduction, the A3143. For either, Anker's quality and customer support are among the best in the industry.
text_fidelity_b: Anker Soundcore Bluetooth Speaker with 24-Hour Playtime, 66-Feet Bluetooth Range & Built-in Mic, Dual-Driver Portable Wireless Speaker with Low Harmonic Distortion and Superior Sound - Blue

Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory I'm normally an ear bud user since I've never been able to find an over the ear headset that was comfortable to wear for more than 10 minutes or so at a time. Well, I found one - these are undoubtable the most comfortable headphones I've ever used. Just a dream to wear even for extended periods of time. Light, cushy, just right. And they look so elegant - a nice change from the sparse industrial look that electronics often have.

Construction quality seems very good, especially the cord (a common point of failure for me with any type of earphones). It comes with the regular and mini size plugs.

The sound quality is absolutly top-notch. I'm not an audiophile, so I can't throw out the phrases and jargon I typically read in audio discussion boards and magazines (well, I can throw them out, but not with any semblance of knowing what I'm taking about). So suffice it to say that I can't imagine anyone not being very pleased with the quality of sound using these and a MP3 player or an iPad (the two devices I've used with them so far). I've been absolutely amazed at how great these sound.

My only complaint is the lack of sound isolation. Outside sounds can easily be heard. Sometimes that's good, but most of the time I prefer to be isolated from whatever else is playing in the house. I'm finding I reach for these more often when I'm in a quiet environment, and use ear buds when there's a lot of noise about (with me defining noise as any type of music I don't care for).

With the caveat of the lack of sound blocking, these should absolutely be on your short list if you're looking for a comfortable, great sounding pair of earphones.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser HD 598 Over-Ear Headphones - Ivory

text_fidelity_a:
Bragi - The Dash Truly Wireless Smart Earphones I've recently purchased this BT headset and the first thing I did was install the latest firmware due to the reviews I've read. While it does most of what they advertise the BT connectivity is really poor unless you hold the phone in a stationary visible position from your phone or while it's stationary on a table. If you put it in your pocket or even in your hand with a normal hand swing the sound stutters and is not worth using. I've purchased a 60 dollar pair of similar BT ear buds without all the extra features but it sure does work reliably in a way you would expect any headset to work. I've written their technical support for assistance and this is what they told me after a few emails back and forth explaining my issue and running their tests. Here is their final reply, I didn't put in the agents name as to not hold the agent responsible directly for this issue.

(Bragi)
Apr 5, 10:26 CEST
Hello Derek

Thanks for getting back to us with the results of your test.

I understand The Black Dash has some issues when being connected to an external device via Bluetooth, specifically when using it outside. In certain cases we have had a few customers who experienced similar issues like you. As you performed the range test and got a positive result, we can confidently say that your unit's Bluetooth hardware is generally working correctly.

Nonetheless, this is not an excuse for your Bluetooth dropouts. Bluetooth, in general is a technology that offers us the possibility to pair The Black Dash to many different devices, due to the technology's widespread usage. Never the less, it is also a technology that comes with disadvantages. One of those is the actual dependency of the surroundings as you discovered already. That actually means that Bluetooth works very well in closed surroundings where you have surfaces that reflect the Bluetooth signals. However, when being outside with no walls at all, the Bluetooth range very much varies. Having your external device in your right side pockets, your The Black Dash should work independently from the outside surroundings.

Again, this is not an excuse for your Bluetooth dropouts, but rather an explanation for this behavior. Furthermore, we are doing our best to regulate Bluetooth performance with our firmware settings, and every update should actually improve Bluetooth performance.
We hope you can understand that.

All the best,
(Agent name)& your Team Bragi​​​​​​
text_fidelity_b: Bragi - The Dash Truly Wireless Smart Earphones

text_fidelity_a:
3M Quiet Space Headphones, Bluetooth Headphones, Wireless Headphones, 1 Pair Most of the headphones with which I have worked have been active noise canceling (ANC) phones so I know a lot about those, but I also have other headphones too that I like. I was unaware that 3M even had headphones, and I was also unsure what their "Quiet Space" was all about. It's an interesting solution that works fairly well. Overall, these are good phones, though there's one area that could use some slight improvement and that's the sound profile.

These are over-the-ear phones and they are actually quite comfortable. I like how they feel on my head - they fit snugly and I can tilt my head without losing these phones, but they don't clamp down super tight either.

Build-wise, these are more substantial than the price suggests. I like the size adjustment in particular which is designed to last and should not fatigue with use.

I powered these on and they quickly paired and connected to my laptop. The range is good and I was able to walk a fair distance away without losing the connection or having the sound get crackly or having it skip. With no feed coming to them they eventually powered themselves off, saving battery but potentially frustrating the wearer if this is unexpected.

Just putting these on I was surprised by the amount of noise isolation. Without even turning these on they drastically reduced the ambient noise in the room, even effectively blocking out the sound of a running fan. I have had very few headphones that have as effective sound isolation as these, and that's a huge plus right out of the gate. The Quiet Space function adds to this, but not like ANC phones - it injects white noise into the cans so all you hear is a gentle but constant hiss that overrides most other noises. It's not deathly quiet with these on, but you won't hear most other sounds in the area when they're producing white noise. This is a very different approach to sound cancellation and it works.

The sound profile is the one area where these phones could use a little improvement, though these are not terrible and are better than some big-name phones I have used. The bass is not overdriven but it is not muted either, and this is refreshing since most manufacturers overdrive the bass. The highs are clear, though not shrill. The midrange, however, is flat to the point that music can sound slightly hollow. It's an easy fix with an equalizer and is better than one particular big-name manufacturer's similar flaw.

I like these phones and will be working with them more. They take a different approach to dealing with ambient noise and surrounding distractions than what ANC phones use, and they seem to work well. They're well made, comfortable and reasonably priced.
text_fidelity_b: 3M Quiet Space Headphones, Bluetooth Headphones, Wireless Headphones, 1 Pair

text_fidelity_a:
Roku Premiere - HD and 4K UHD Streaming Media Player The Roku Premiere player is easy to set up and has a well-designed user interface that requires no reference to a user manual. I connected it to the tv (using an HDMI cable), plugged it in, turned on the tv and selected the appropriate source. I was disappointed that there was no option to plug in a network cable for a wired connection (like there is for the Fire TV box; you have to go up to the Premiere+ to get that port). This might be a concern for anyone with a weak or problematic wifi signal.

The initialization was fairly simple: language selection, wifi connection (it supports AC as well as N), automatic detection of the tv display type, automatic software update, then a separate session on the computer to register the device and create a Roku account. I had another disappointment here: the account creation requires the entry of payment info, either credit card or Paypal. If I want to use the box just to watch my subscribed services, such as Netflix and Amazon, there's no reason for me to give Roku any payment information at all, it just increases the risk of malicious use. (If you really don't like this, you can sign up using a Paypal account, then go back into your Paypal account and rescind the Roku permissions.)

After that it was all plain sailing, and I had no complaints: streaming video was clear and glitch-free, the sound was good. All in all, a very nice streaming box for a reasonable price. For my money, however, I would consider upgrading to the Premiere+. Or, the Fire TV box, which is what I normally use at home.
text_fidelity_b: Roku Premiere - HD and 4K UHD Streaming Media Player

text_fidelity_a:
Canon EF-S 55-250mm F4-5.6 IS STM Lens with UV Protection Filter - 58 mm I purchased this lens on Amazon offered by a gray market vendor for $140 (new!). Gray Market means there is no USA Warranty. I haven't tried to see if it is eligible, but I assume it would not be. As of this writing (10/12/2014), that vendor, CD Supply, is still offering the lens - though now for $170. Still an incredible deal for this lens which came new in the standard Canon box with manual etc. (If it isn't warranteed - I can buy another and still be about the price of just one at regular price).

The lens itself: I was pleasantly surprised. I could have purchased it in my kit with the 70D camera, but wasn't really interested. For $140 - what the heck. The photos are sharper than from the kit 18-135mm STM IS lens in my opinion (and that's a pretty decent lens as kit lenses go). It is very small and light weight for a pretty long lens - especially on a crop sensor.
BONUS: Macro. It actually can get pretty decent magnification. Something like 1/4:1 from a pretty good distance at 250mm.
Plus it works great with extension tubes. I've used it with 12mm and 26mm (not together) and it worked great. Even autofocus - though I wouldn't recommend that for Macro.

Negatives (though - again - if you get it for cheap, these are quibbles):
- No lens hood provided. Buy a knock off on Amazon for $13
- Not a super bright lens. You're going to need some decent sunlight or a good flash with this. It ramps up to f/5 minimum pretty quick and f/5.6 not too long after that. Only the widest shots will get F/4.
- Pretty cheaply built (but it's a cheap lens!)
text_fidelity_b: Canon EF-S 55-250mm F4-5.6 IS STM Lens with UV Protection Filter - 58 mm

text_fidelity_a:
ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In Ok, I have to admit I'm pretty impressed with this little camera. At first I thought I had to use the Haven subscription, especially after reading the reviews here which said it is necessary. I was kind of bummed about that at first but it turns out this is really useful even without! Sure, being able to record videos and store them in the cloud require a subscription as well as many of the advanced features, but you can still "arm" the camera to snap a photo and alert your phone when it detects motion, which it does splendidly even without a sub. The way I currently use it, it alerts my phone and I can then go to the live view and see and even interact with who is there (talk feature is really cool!).
On top of that, I set ours up with Amazon's Alexa voice service and it is EXTREMELY COOL! I think the speaker seems a bit louder than an Echo Dot, which surprised me. I'm mounting ours by the front porch so we can see people come to the door and interact with them, but we can also use it to play music via Amazon's Alexa when just sitting on the porch drinking coffee. That's an amazing perk that I wasn't expecting before we got it!
I do wish you could combine it with device music groups in Alexa (so I could say, for example, play this song on the everywhere group and it will play inside on our Echo and out on the porch with the Ecobee), but sadly only echo devices can be grouped. That's OK, I knew that before getting this as other devices in our home can't be grouped either (Facebook Portal or Kindles, for example).
If you want to spring for the subscription service, there's a TON of goodies and advanced features beyond even the cloud storage things. But even without that, the live view and photo motion alerts combined with the voice assistant / Alexa integration makes it worth it even just for the hardware alone!
text_fidelity_b: ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In

text_fidelity_a:
Meta Portal - Smart Video Calling for the Home with 10” Touch Screen Display - White We've been using an older first generation Portal and like it very much. I was not expecting to be so impressed with this one, but wow have they managed to improve almost everything about the original! It still has the very cool zoom-and-pan style camera feature that follows the subject, as well as all the fun filters and of course my kids' favorite, story time... but the polish and style of this unit is really premium. The speaker is fantastic and LOUD if you want it to be. The clarity and bass rivals my bookshelf speakers so well, sometimes the kids play music off it and I could have sworn they were using the speakers in the living room. But the biggest improvement over the previous generation is the ability to run off battery power and move around. The "portable portal" honestly makes so much sense, I wonder why the original stationary style ones came out first!
Make no mistake, it is NOT a tablet, it is not thin and won't fit in an attaché case nicely. It is wedge-shaped making it stand easily at an ideal angle, and even has a cut-out handle to pick it up and carry it to a better location for video chat. This is great for bringing it to wherever my kids happen to be congregating currently, and it can be put back up on the shelf when done to charge. Like the original Portals, it has Alexa built in and can act as an Echo for most things, however it is very tied into Facebook's ecosystem. That means that although it seems to run something akin to Android behind the scenes, this is NOT going to offer a standard App store, and even things like Youtube are not available for it (licensing issues with Google I'd suppose). However there is a browser, and you can navigate to YouTube and play it from the website just fine, although a proper app would be much easier to navigate. It does have Plex support, which I found interesting since I have a Plex server. I never thought I'd find Plex available where Youtube is not! Meanwhile, between Youtube in the browser, Amazon Music through Alexa and content on Plex, there are plenty of ways to make it a music streamer on that glorious better-than-it-should-sound speaker. And the camera works just as well if not better than the OG Portal!
Calls over FB Messenger or Whatsapp work well, and of course the camera / mic not only have a switch to toggle, but the camera has a physical cover that can slide over the lens in case you don't trust Facebook not to snoop. But that's another story.
All things considered, this is a solid product.
text_fidelity_b: Meta Portal - Smart Video Calling for the Home with 10” Touch Screen Display - White

LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports A good laptop chiller pad becomes important when you run a lot of graphics-intensive games or if you are doing anything requiring the CPU to run a heavy load. Heat is the enemy of a computer system and the fastest way to a dead laptop is to not deal with heat issues when there’s a problem. I had a chill pad some time ago and it was sub-par. This one by LotFancy is much better and it does a good job.

First off, this is a big chill pad, the same basic dimensions as my laptop but much thicker. I have a 15.6" laptop and this pad is almost a perfect and exact fit, with only a narrow area in the back that extends past the end of the laptop. If you want a small and petite chill pad, this is not the one you want. It does incline too with a metal bar and slots in the case so that the laptop can be angled up. This actually is good for exposing it to even more air.

This chill pad connects to a USB port so it can either be plugged into a port on the computer or into a hub. There are two ports on it and both seem to be the same in terms of how the pad operates. That is, the pad operates at the same speed regardless of which port is used. There are also two buttons on the pad for turning it on. One turns on the larger fan in the middle, and the other turns on all the other fans. Two green LEDs next to those buttons indicate that the pad is powered on and working.

This pad moves a lot of air and it does a good job of cooling the laptop. But, it does so very quietly which is a huge plus. I have it set up in my home office and the pad makes about as much noise as a desktop computer, maybe a little less. The sound it makes is a gentle hum.

When powered on each fan has a bright blue LED in it. While they look cool when there’s no laptop on the pad, they’re all but invisible when the laptop is sitting on top. There isn’t even much of a glow coming from the pad. I turned on the pad, turned out all of the lights and the glow from the laptop screen was enough to overpower any light that might have come from the pad. Except for the low hum I wouldn’t know it was even turned on.

This is a good chill pad. It works quietly and it moves a lot of air. Compared to other chill pads I have used this one is very good and I am happy to recommend it.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports

I spend a lot of my time listening to podcasts while I do a 1.5 hr drive to work. In the past, I used to just sit my telephone in a cradle and turn the volume up, but at freeway speeds the ambient noise was enough to make it hard to hear the sound coming from the phone's speaker.

This product charges in your cigarette lighter and allows you to connect your phone to the car radio via bluetooth. You then have to pick a radio station that is not carrying a broadcast and set the control on the bluetooth FM to the same station. All of this sounds like a lot while I'm typing it out, but it goes quickly. However, I do highly recommend that you make sure the radio is set up correctly before you start driving. There are enough accidents caused by texting, and this does represent another potential driving distraction. If you set this item up while parked, it is very useful, but if you try to do it on the roll, then it could be dangerous...fair warning.

Once you have your phone connected to your car speaker system you can listen to your own music, podcasts, etc. It is a little bit of a problem when somebody calls you, however, because the device doesn't automatically un-pair when there is a call. I found I usually had to call people back if I got a phone call. Not a huge issue really.

There is also a mini flash card slot on this device so you could play your music directly from that.

Really a good product. I received a complimentary sample in exchange for an honest review.

The key to speeds like that is not looking at the keyboard, ever. When I received this keyboard skin (in return for my honest review) and put it on my MacBook Pro 15" Retina, I realized why my typing speed has slowed down so much. It's because I always seem to be looking at the keyboard! And having this skin on made me have to unlearn this bad behavior. Now I'm trying to look at it only when I can't remember a keyboard shortcut and need to refer to the key tops for instructions. This is like mini flashcards, a proven learning tool.

Once I got used to how different it is not to be looking at the keyboard all the time, I'm now getting used to the slightly different feel of typing on the skin. It's really a subtle difference. The skin fits exceptionally well, and it's great to know I'm not getting dust and dog hair floating into the keys; also, I don't have to worry quite so much about spilling coffee into the keyboard. GreatShield (3 Pack) Ultra Anti-Glare (Matte) Clear Screen Protector Film for Amazon Kindle Fire (Does Not Fit Kindle Fire HD) I keep being offered this product to review through the "Your Review Helped" emails I get, even though I've already reviewed it through Vine, so I'll take this opportunity to offer an update. The screen smudges easily with the Great Shield protector applied, and it's hard to clean it. I've subsequently had an opportunity to review the Moshi product, and it is hands-down the best of the two. The clarity of the Moshi screen is better than the Great Shield, and it's easier to apply. I've accordingly bumped the Great Shield down to three stars now that I have something better for comparison.

Original review through Amazon Vine:

Okay, like some other reviewers, I had a frustrating experience getting this anti-glare screen protector installed properly on my Kindle Fire. When you buy this three-pack, figure they are giving you two hands-on lessons in how to install it! (Considering I paid over twice as much for just one Zagg screen protector for my Kindle 2, the price for this Fosmon product is still very reasonable.) I had read all the reviews and warnings before I began, and I still ruined my first two.

First, who lives in a "dust-free environment"? You have to be very careful. You should first shake any dust off the protector itself; after I'd failed to install the first two, I used one of the wipes that came with them to wipe down both sides of my last protector to clear it of all packing dust that it arrived with. Then clean your Fire screen, including the cracks around the sides of the screen. Clean it again. And again.

My first effort went very well until I went to remove the #2 (face) plastic. I didn't realize I had to very slowly pull up on the tab to get the top piece started coming away from the actual shield protector before pulling—so I pulled the whole thing off! One down, two to go. On my second effort, I didn't quite get the protector perfectly positioned so I had a very slight overlap on the right-hand side, resulting in a large unattached area. Unusable. The third time, I folded the #1 plastic down halfway, just so I could hold the protector flat above my Fire and not touch the actual protector (to avoid fingerprints), edged the upper right corner in perfectly straight, anchored it across the top, and then let the protector kind of glide itself onto the screen as I pulled off the remaining #1 plastic. I had some larger bubbled areas, but I did not try to use the little cardboard piece to squeegee them out; I used my thumbs to press outward toward the nearest edge. This gave me a near-perfect installation. I carefully removed the #2 plastic, slipped my Fire back into its [[ASIN:B005QBK5V2 rooCASE Dual-View Multi Angle (Black) 100% Genuine Leather Leather Folio Case Cover for Amazon Kindle Fire 7-Inch Android Tablet]], tucked one of the little squares of screen-cleaning cloth behind the Fire for later cleaning use if needed, and it was all good to go.

After regularly fighting the glare from my Kindle Fire, it took me a little while for my eyes to adjust to the difference with the anti-glare shield protector in place, but I LIKE it! Reading is now easier on my eyes, and my [[ASIN:B005EM6IAA GreatShield 2-in-1 Ballpoint Pen and Capacitive Touchscreen Stylus for Amazon Kindle Fire Tablet]] seems to be working with more precision than it was before. Despite the hassles, I do recommend this product and I'm glad I've got it.
text_fidelity_b: GreatShield (3 Pack) Ultra Anti-Glare (Matte) Clear Screen Protector Film for Amazon Kindle Fire (Does Not Fit Kindle Fire HD)

text_fidelity_a: Logitech Harmony One Universal Remote with Color Touchscreen (Discontinued by Manufacturer) In the beginning, you will love this remote. But it will break. Guaranteed. We had one stop working, and Logitech replaced it. We dropped the replacement once (just from coffee table to floor, but it's fragile!) and the screen cracked. We were upset that it broke so easily but knew it was damage not covered by warranty, so we didn't submit a claim. We figured we'd just had a freak accident/bad luck, and bought a third one. One day I picked that one up and the screen was whited out. Over the next few days, black started to seep across the screen from one edge. By the time I had to send a picture of the remote to Logitech for our warranty claim, you could see cracks at the edge. That remote was never dropped. My best guess it that I set it down on the side table as though it were a remote, not a Faberge egg. Logitech refuses to honor their warranty. It's like beating your head against a wall. Lots of "I understand you must be frustrated," and no actual help. Not acceptable for a product that costs so much. Mine is not the only review that says this -- please believe it! Unless you have the money to buy a new one every 6 months (the longest that one of our three Harmony Ones has ever lasted), just don't do it.

Verso Prologue Case Cover for Kindle Fire, Tan (does not fit Kindle Fire HD) At first glance, this appears to be an elegant folio cover for tablets; it has an authentic-looking antique book design with embossing on the faux leather, some "gold" leafing, and real top-stitching, and it fits nicely on a book shelf (great disguise if you think you need to hide your device for whatever reason). While the design is lovely and the black microfiber supposedly prevents your screen from getting scratched, the way the tablet is held in is by four elastic straps that do an ok job, but I feel in time will wear out. Because of that concern, the design gets 4/5 stars

The function of this folio is to give the tablet a different look and ease of portability without fear of it breaking. It also helps serve as a dust cover for those who have tablets that don't always use them. This is not made for all terrain, though it's good and light weight enough for public transport. Parks and other minor recreational places are ok. I wouldn't take this folio camping or to the beach do to fear of destroying both the folio and tablet. Even though there is a cover there is a minor opening that doesn't really stay closed with the tablet in it. This folio doesn't really appear to protect a tablet from accidental drops. For every day use, this gets a 3.5/5, and for not-so every day use (rougher environments), it's closer to 1/5, so bear that in mind when deciding what case to buy.

The positive thing about this folio is that it fits most 7.1 inch tablets It did fit the Galaxy Tab 7.1 and the original kindle with keyboard. I would recommend an accessories pack to go along with the folio, since screen protector is a must! Over all for a folio I would give it 3.5/5 rounded up to 4. While is is beautiful, it only keeps to the basics of what a tablet user needs.
text_fidelity_b: Verso Prologue Case Cover for Kindle Fire, Tan (does not fit Kindle Fire HD)

Fujifilm Instax Wide 300 Instant Film Camera (Black) Boy! does this camera remind me of my old Polaroid Square Shooter. This camera is NOTHING like your iPhone camera as it's big, and totally analog except for the film counter on the back. I love it when the motor runs and film comes sliding out - a sound I well remember. I think the hardest thing about using this camera was getting the shoulder strap put on, other than that it's very easy to use. Though it is on the big side, it doesn't weigh much and the view finder and shutter button are pretty much intuitive. I'm left handed so holding it like a right-hander took a little getting used too, but it's not a problem for me. This camera is made for right-handers so those who are very much left-handed might not like the way you have to hold it, and the shutter button is on the right side front. It has flash and you can adjust the light/dark and distance to you subject with minimal effort.

Loading the film was easy, aiming at my subject was easy, the shutter button was easy to depress and everything is/was easy. The close-up adapter looks like there's no way it will attach itself to the lens, but somehow it does. I took one close-up of my dog but the picture didn't turn out very good because she moved away right when I hit the shutter button-but that's typical for her. I haven't taken a "selfie" yet but it seems like it will be easy to do.

The color development of the film is pretty good. I took a wide angle picture of my raised garden beds and I was able to get all of them in the picture and the various green colors were vivid. I also took a picture of the front of our house, and though I had to still walk across the street to our neighbor's driveway to get the entire house in the view finder, the picture turned out nice. Again, the colors were bright and vivid. It got the entire house plus some area on both sides. In the past with my other cameras I would have to get further away or be happy with just most of the house in the picture so it's real nice to get the whole thing with room to spare.

The film is kind of pricey. For a pack of 40 pictures it costs around $34.00. I figured it would be kind of expensive and I hope the price of the film goes down some. This is a comfort camera for those of us who grew up with Polaroids. It may be that since we are living in highly uncertain and stressful times, having a camera like this is a cool blast from the past and may make us just feel better having one like this, plus it takes nice pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Fujifilm Instax Wide 300 Instant Film Camera (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
1MORE Quad Driver in-Ear Earphones Hi-Res High Fidelity Headphones Warm Bass, Spacious Reproduction, High Resolution, Mic in-Line Remote Smartphones/PC/Tablet - Silver/Gray I am not an audiophile by any means. I have Rockbox installed on my iPod video classic with a FiiO amp attached, all loaded with FLAC tunes. I listen to Spotify at work. That's the extent of my musical needs.
I have Audio-Technica headphones, and dream of some day owning custom Kaisers. That's my background.

I was pretty excited to get these. Right after ordering, I watched a few YouTube videos on them, and read up on Head-Fi. For the price, 1More seems to deliver outstanding products. Needless to say, I was pretty excited.

The box finally came and I was found to be very impressed with the presentation. You get a nice, magnetic box housing the IEMs, a leather(ette?) pouch, and multiple choices of ear piece tips. For starters, I found that the ear piece tips pre-attached to the IEMs were the most fitted for me, but I still do not find them perfect. They slide down a bit when in my ear, so there is some loss of sound. I will have to buy some aftermarket ones.

The microphone is also sub-par. This is the first time I've used a mic with headphones, and most of my calls could not catch my voice properly. I would get complaints that I sounded muffled or far away, and so I've resorted to using the phone mic most of the time. The mic buttons work flawlessly for playback features, however.

As for the sound, it's fantastic. With four drivers, I can hear so much more--and so many more flaws! I usually transfer music files into FLAC, and so I have pretty good sources for music. I've been using both my Samsung Galaxy S5 and Rockboxed iPod Video (equipped with a Fiio E11), and the sounds are great, but I'm noticing some files that weren't transferred correctly. I cannot connect to my computer speakers at work as the speakers do not have enough power to juice up the Quads, so be sure you have a more recent device or one with enough power to drive these IEMs.

I also use them on my Wii U's GamePad for Breath of the Wild, and they're actually better than my Audio-Technicas, even with the sliding ear tips. I hear a lot more, and sound is very important in the game.

All in all, amazing value for the price. The ear tip issue is more personal as my ears simply don't fit perfectly any of the ones provided, but I do wish the mic worked better.
text_fidelity_b: 1MORE Quad Driver in-Ear Earphones Hi-Res High Fidelity Headphones Warm Bass, Spacious Reproduction, High Resolution, Mic in-Line Remote Smartphones/PC/Tablet - Silver/Gray

text_fidelity_a:
Rosewill 3.5 Inch Hard Drive Enclosure to USB 3.0 / eSATA. External Hard Drive Case Aluminum Body, Built-in Cooling Fan and Fan Switch. Support 3.5” SATA III / II / I Hard Drive up to 6TB and UASP function. Wouldn't recognize on the eSATA port. It would detect the HDD, but would not format nor store data. I thought it would be plug and play. I submitted a return request (which the seller approved), but after extensive Googling, discovered how to make it work on my machine.

1) For Windows 7 (I think Windows 10 may not have this issue), make sure you have the registry entry to allow AHCI.
2) In BIOS, make sure your boot devices are in proper order.
3) In BIOS, update RAID configuration to AHCI.

After that, it is operating as expected.
text_fidelity_b: Rosewill 3.5 Inch Hard Drive Enclosure to USB 3.0 / eSATA. External Hard Drive Case Aluminum Body, Built-in Cooling Fan and Fan Switch. Support 3.5” SATA III / II / I Hard Drive up to 6TB and UASP function.

Bliksem SSD 128GB SATA III 6Gb/s Internal Solid State Drive 2.5″ 7mm(0.28″) 3D NAND TLC Chip Up to 550 Mb/s for Laptop and Pc KD650 (Black 128GB) This is a great CHEAP sata solid state drive. I want to emphasize that this is CHEAP- it is not going to be a speed demon, and it's not large enough to be a main storage drive to house mission-critical data. But it seems to deliver consistently over 400mbps in benchmark tests, which is more than enough to get the benefits of it over a mechanical drive in a SATA setup.
I can't vouch for the longevity of a brand I've never heard of, but again... the value here is the insanely low price of entry. That makes it great for refurbishing an old laptop or perhaps turning older hardware into a chrome book or a closet file server at home. I like to use it in HDMI recording devices such as an Atmos Ninja, as I can edit footage directly off the drive (it's fast enough!) when plugged into my computer, and it's nice to have a backup from my camera's SD card slot when recording events. If the drive dies one day, nothing major will have been lost. For what it is, so far I am impressed, just have realistic expectations for what you can use it for. I probably would not use this for my main computer C drive if only because it is a laughably small amount of storage. But as a fast SSD that uses legacy SATA connections, it definitely has uses!

Crucial Ballistix RGB 3200 MHz DDR4 DRAM Desktop Gaming Memory Kit 32GB (16GBx2) CL16 BL2K16G32C16U4BL (Black) These sticks are a hair faster than my previous DIMMs, which were also rated with a 3200mhz XMP profile. I actually really like the LEDs on them because I happen to have an MSI motherboard that recognized them instantly and let me control the lights via their Mystic Light setup. The glow adds a cool look to the case, and can also be used to keep an eye on CPU temp (you can have the colors change as the CPU temp rises). The ones I got were 16-18-18-36 timings, which actually were close enough to my G.Skill ram that I could combine them and get pretty good performance out of both kits together.
The only thing I didn't like, however, is how the height was difficult to work around my heat sync. I had to switch which DIMM slots I used because the one closest to my cooling system didn't have enough height clearance to fit. Thankfully my other RAM could slide in there and I now have these LED ones in the other 2 slots. So, just keep that in mind if you have a tight space and a large heat pipe system, you might need shorter DIMMs that forgo the LED.
I'm actually quite happy that I was able to make this work, there was a moment in which I was almost going to give up. If they'll fit in your setup, I'd say they are pretty cool looking and plenty fast for a modern Mobo.
text_fidelity_b: Crucial Ballistix RGB 3200 MHz DDR4 DRAM Desktop Gaming Memory Kit 32GB (16GBx2) CL16 BL2K16G32C16U4BL (Black)

Amazon Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" Standing Leather Origami Case (will only fit Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" - 3rd Generation), Red I had the very first kindle...with a red leather first gen case. I was really excited to get the new hdx 8.9" kindle and a new red leather case. These origami cases seem like a good idea. But if you have them sitting on any kind of slightly slick surface or slightly inclined surface, it won't stand up. The function of the "origami" part is a little complicated, but the pictures help. Initially it is it very stiff and hard to "fold". After a few uses it loosens up which makes setting up the "standing" position a little easier, but it still resists the action and as I mentioned, slips. I was thinking a little rubber edge all around the case edge would help some. The case "attaches" to the kindle via magnets and turns your kindle on automatically when you open the case, off when up close it. On the up side, I definitely prefer the feel of the leather case as opposed to the plastic one. Sadly neither case really functions as it should for standing. However it will provide some protection for the glass which is a pretty good size now. In addition to the magnet set in, there is are outer power and volume buttons. They are in good locations and I have not hit them accidently. In fact those buttons are quite handy.
I just wish they'd put more thought into actual function and less into "wow this looks cool" on the stand part.
Hope this helps some. I have not found a great alternative yet, but I will keep looking and update this review if I find one.
text_fidelity_b: Amazon Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" Standing Leather Origami Case (will only fit Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" - 3rd Generation), Red

- regarding payments: I have a Piper camera that records up to 1,000 24s videos for free, overwriting after that. It works great. It always worked. Why Ring enforce additional payment is mind-blowing considering what is available on the market.

UPDATE: had to completely disable the motion sensor, the false positives were driving me crazy. Not paying the monthly fee. It's too many clicks to get to the screen when somebody actually pushes the button.
Avoid this product and wait for competitors to come up with something better.
UPDATE 2: Now this piece of crap will not enter live view.
