Stellar Labs,Outdoor FM Antenna OMNIDIRECTIONAL 9/12/2015
Final Review:
Have now completed the installation and hookup of this antenna. The first test was to listen to Mixed Bag, 90.7 FM which was always full of static. Now this station comes in crystal clear, loud, and strong. Note that I decided to mount this antenna on the side of my house, just beneath the peak of my low roof facing the back yard. I had a quantity of twin 300 ohm cable which I wanted to use. Using a 300ohm/75ohm converter, I simply attached the end of the cable to the two 300ohm screws, protecting the connection with electrical tape. I measured and fabricated a wood mounting plate (see photo) and then screwed the mast bracket to it from the back. The wooden support board was then lag screwed, in turn, to the outside of my house just below the peak using 5" long screws. I then installed the antenna and mast, after reversing it. It now extends upwards vertically yet does not interfere with the roof line. The versatility of the mast permitted me to accomplish that.

(This review is preliminary. I assembled the antenna but am not yet ready to install it.
Assembly tips:

- Both curved antenna segments are secured to the antenna cross bar with the supplied hardware.
- The ends of one (bottom) segment are held in place with two phillips head screws. First, remove the curved metal clamp. line up the holes in the segment and, maintaining hand pressure on each segment end to ensure that it is seated firmly into it's curved metal seat, insert each screw and secure. Do not over tighten these fasteners. This is the "bottom" of the antenna, opposite the 75 ohm connector side. Attach one leg of the segment at a time.
- The ends of the second (top) segment are held in place with two hex head nuts. You will note that each nut is topped with a rubber 'O' ring. This is used to keep the nuts from threading off until assembly. Do not attempt to re-use these as they are not spacers or washers.
- Again, seat the ends of the antenna segment firmly in place, aligning the holes over the studs. Holding down the segment, install each nut. Do not over tighten these nuts.
- The closed loop ends of each antenna segment may now be gently guided in front of the black plastic locking clips. Once the looped ends are in position, firmly, yet carefully snap them into place. The circular antenna shape has now been completed. If assembled patiently and slowly, damage should not occur to the antenna.)
text_fidelity_b: Stellar Labs,Outdoor FM Antenna OMNIDIRECTIONAL

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device I am not the target demographic for this device: middle-aged empty nester who loves to watch sci-fi, thrillers, and horror. I have a number of these brilliantly simple, highly configurable lights. They are perfect in the bedroom where, depending on our intended mood, a variety of different colors or modes might be appropriate. I have two in the living room, hiding behind tropical plants at a 3' height, on either side of the big screen, about 5 feet away on each side. I have a routine set up to turn off all the lights in the room and engage campfire mode in both lights at 45% brightness with a single keyword. Voila--instant torchlight in the jungle (or romantic candlelight - take your pick). I am a colossal LOST fan, and this lighting is perfect for watching LOST, or anything scary or dark. And if I need a different effect, that's only a few words away.

The simplicity with which these set up and configure themselves is so good it makes Apple products jealous. If you have an Alexa on your Wi-Fi network, simply plug the Glow in to a power source, open the Alexa app on your phone, and the light will auto-connect to your network and add itself to Alexa. It will then prompt you to configure it with a name and add it to any groups, etc. Utterly simple. If the setup fails, it might ask you to scan the barcode on the back of the booklet it came with to get it going, but this has not been my experience - they have all self-configured and join the network seamlessly.

For those of you complaining this does not have a mic and speaker - folks, it works WITH an Echo device. It is a light - that's it. If Amazon built Alexa mics and speakers into this it would cost double--and I am positive they are developing just such a light ...for which you will pay $60+.

Normally, these are $30/ea, but they were 45% off on Prime Day, so I added a few more. There are indeed cheaper (and much more expensive) smart mood lights on the market, but if you run Alexa at home, this is hands down the best way to do it. Seamless.

It baffles me that Amazon does not have a whole range of lighting products which work exactly like this. They easily could. Give me one of these on a larger scale (12-15") and make it weatherproof for outside on the patio, please.
text_fidelity_b: Echo Glow - Multicolor smart lamp, a Certified for Humans Device – Requires compatible Alexa device

eufy Security Indoor Cam E220, Pan & Tilt, Indoor Security Camera, 2K - 3 MP Wi-Fi Plug-in, Voice Assistant Compatibility, Night Vision, Motion Tracking, HomeBase 3 Compatible, Motion Only Alert Purchased two of these Eufy 2K cams to test out and determine if they're good enough to replace the Wyze cams. These Eufy cams definitely capture higher resolution, more detailed videos compared to the Wyze cam v2. The pan and tilt feature is great when I want to remotely check different parts of an area and the pan/tilt action is very silent. You can set the cam to automatically track/follow motion when it's detected. The amount of time it takes to go to live view on a cam is within a couple of seconds and the alerts for motion is definitely faster than the Wyze cam v2. The time from me waving my hand in front of the cam and getting an alert on my phone is about 3 seconds or less.

I did experience issues with one Eufy cam where it would randomly start panning by itself and would do a 360 degree pan. The Eufy app works overall, but I did notice several times I had connection issues when trying to live view, but this issue also happens on Wyze cams, too.

You can set the Eufy cam to record only when motion or sound is detected or set the cam to continuous recording. If you choose continuous recording the video resolution will be reduced to 1080p resolution. For motion recording you can set up activity zones (specific areas you want to detect motion), adjust motion detection sensitivity, detect people, detect pets, and detect all other motion. Eufy's app is still missing the ability to view multiple live views of cams at the same time, which is a shame and hopefully they have a software update for that.

Overall, the Eufy 2k cam has great video quality, the pan/tilt motion is useful and silent, has a lot of features, and the price is competitive. They go on sale from time to time, so if you're not in a hurry then I'd wait for a sale.

text_fidelity_a: Amazon Basics SDHC Class 4 16GB Secure Digital Card the plus to this card is obvious--it has a large capacity.  The con is that it is a little slow in picture-taking.  Depending on what you're looking for, you may be happy or dissatisfied. Picture-taking was a different story; there was a noticeable lag in taking still photos. I wouldn't dismiss this card for that reason, however, unless a difference of a second or so will matter to you.  Most of my still picture taking on vacation is done with a larger point and shoot Canon IS, so the lag time with the little camera didn't matter much to me as I either used it mostly for video as mentioned or took stills of landscape or posed photos.  To be honest, I prefer not to use such a large capacity card for photos anyway as I have a fear of something going wrong with the card and losing hundreds of photos as opposed to a few videos.  So I'm happy to keep this in the little compact video camera and snap the occasional slow photo. I wouldn't put it in my Canon for the above reason and also because the photos I take with that I'd be more concerned about the sluggish picture-taking.  Be selective about how you use it, and I think you'll be more than satisfied

So they must have made some useful advances in the relevant technology in the four years since I last purchased a transmitter from them.

I have tested this transmitter with multiple Bluetooth headphones that I own, and in each case, the Bluetooth connects seamlessly. I like the fact that the transmitter speaks and lets me know when the Bluetooth has connected. And a split second after that, the sound from my TV comes through my Bluetooth headphones. My old Avantree transmitter had neither of those abilities. It would take up to 2 minutes to get it connected to my Bluetooth headphones after multiple tries, and the sound's clarity and volume weren't nearly as good.

As was the case with my previous transmitter, this one can handle multiple Bluetooth headphones at the same time. So far I have only attempted transmission with two at a time.

Finally, the appearance of this transmitter is much fancier than the old one. I will admit that it is about three times larger than the old one, but that is not really a problem for me, because the old one was tiny and this one is still conveniently small. It has some cute, space-age looking little antennas on it that the other one didn't have, which may partially account for why it works so much better.

All in all, I am very pleased with this purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Avantree Oasis B Bluetooth 5.0 Transmitter Receiver for TV, Home Stereo Speakers, Bypass Mode, Class 1 Long Range, LED Indicator, Optical AUX RCA, aptX Low Latency Audio Adapter for 2 Headphones

text_fidelity_a:
Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord For the price this is a very nice USB microphone, I would agree with other reviewers that it performs on par with or better than similar competing USB condenser mics in this price range such as Blue Snowball or the Behringer C1.

I do wish it came with more accessories though similar to the non-USB version. The Aokeo AK-60 XLR version comes with a scissor boom arm, shock mount and pop filter for the same price.. so if you do happen to have a compatible audio interface with phantom power then I would recommend the XLR version.

The main annoyance with this mic is that when using it in windows 10 the driver does not have native mic gain control option. In many recording programs you can boost the mic gain via other means but if using this mic for gaming or other purposes through the native drivers then you will have to be very close to the mic to produce adequate volume (ie you pretty much need a boom arm) or otherwise you will need to boost gain via external passthrough program such as APO equalizer. I have also tried this mic in linux and the drivers there do have native gain control.

Overall I do think the sound quality and construction of the mic is good for the price and I would recommend it .. just note that if using windows 10 you will probably either need a boom arm or need to use external software to boost the mic gain. A boom arm is strongly recommended anyways to prevent extraneous noises like keyboard clacking, etc..
text_fidelity_b: Aokeo USB Microphone, Condenser Podcast Microphone for Computer. Suitable for Recording, Gaming, Desktop, Windows, Mac, YouTube, Streaming, Discord

text_fidelity_a: WD 8TB My Book Desktop External Hard Drive, USB 3.0, External HDD with Password Protection and Backup Software - WDBBGB0080HBK-NESN Buyers should note that this drive is formatted in exFAT. Without knowing this, I plugged it in to a running computer and began to transfer some files. The computer was shut down for the night. The next morning, I found that the computer refused to boot up with the new drive installed. Unplugged the drive, and the computer booted up fine. Finally checked the file system. Found it to be exFAT. Moved the files off and re-formatted the drive to NTFS and the problem went away. I suggest anyone purchasing this unit just save yourself the time and trouble and reformat it right out of the box. The software on the drive isn't needed anyway. I have several Western Digital external drives and this is the first one that arrived in a format other than NTFS.

text_fidelity_a:
Lemorele USB C Hub, 10-in-1 USB C Dongle, USB-C Hub Multiport Adapter with HDMI 4K 60Hz, Gigabit Ethernet, 100W Power Delivery, 2 USB 3.0 Ports, SD/TF Card Reader for MacBook Pro/Air Type C Laptops I got this because my laptop has only 3 USB C ports and no standard USB ports. One of them is for power, and I've got a wireless mouse and keyboard, which leaves one port for everything else.
Needless to say, I need a few more ports and also an ethernet connection (RJ45).
The unit comes nicely boxed and for some reason has a bunch of stickers for the flags of various countries. Not sure why, but it's an interesting approach.
It has a lot of ports, an HDMI, RJ45,SD Card and micro SD, 1 USB C, 1 PD, which looks like a USB C, but is a power port, 2 USB 2.0 and 2 USB 3.0.
There is a warning label that says it might get hot (up to 130" F) and thatdevices with power higher than 7.5W are not supported, so check on the things you will be plugging into the hub before you buy it. It also says the PD adapter is under 40W and may not be able to charge all devices through the hub.
So, if you are going to use this to power a bunch of USB devices or charge your phones, it might not work. But if you are just plugging things in like cameras, microphones or drives then it will work fine.
For having all those ports, it's not as large as some others I've used and all in all is a nice hub. If you need more ports, then this is definitely worth considering.
text_fidelity_b: Lemorele USB C Hub, 10-in-1 USB C Dongle, USB-C Hub Multiport Adapter with HDMI 4K 60Hz, Gigabit Ethernet, 100W Power Delivery, 2 USB 3.0 Ports, SD/TF Card Reader for MacBook Pro/Air Type C Laptops

text_fidelity_a:
Emotn C1 Mini WiFi Projector, 1080P Supported Portable Projector, 8500Lux Bluetooth 5.1 200" Movie Projector with HiFi Speaker, 50000H Lamp Life, Compatible with Smartphone/TV Stick/HDMI/USB/VGA/PS4 I must confess and give a shout out- I follow the “phantom of Amazon” as he’s practically reviewed every home projector Ive looked at.. Following his detailed pro/cons lists and why- is what helped me decide. He’s a person in the business and knows his stuff.. So, when HE named this one the best in this price point I took his advice and I’m thrilled I did!!

As one with zero tech skills- I needed “guru advice” about things I didn’t realize or understand. After a few extra “how to” videos for confident (I suggest doing this too, if unsure on anything.) Im so happy set on nightstand or TV tray- it’s truly a perfect height for screen we chose. It’s important to get auto focus BUT, have ability to fine tune by hand- doing so, picture is crystal clear.

Bc our furniture sit on carpet stabilizer let us even up the x1 side that’s 1/4” off from edge of screen. We haven’t used this outside yet- but assuming if on grass.. stabilizer will be a must for sure! With options on auto settings all was solid from picture to color. If connected or told how.. a teen could use with their friend and have confidence to pull this off no prob.!

Read instructions and then SAVE THEM SAFELY IN PLASTIC SLEEVE/BAG!! Hack: we doubled side taped a sleeve to under side of projector- where safe and easy to locate always! 2 Hack: depending on where you’ll use who knows how close to power source you are.. you’ll want to get extension cord to keep with projector.. keep with equipment to avoid any disappointment or avoidable obstacles!!

Blue tooth is the bomb!! If projector/Bluetooth is turned on- it will try to auto sync by invitation- if you follow prompts to do so on device.. it will hold your hand the whole way! Funny to see ME type these things.. but, trust me.. if I can make it thru the process you can x1000!!! Note: we didn’t use an extra speaker with our movie bc, x3 of us could hear just fine from projector alone.. you receive sound out both sides it seems- NICE!! My son played PS4 games using projector and crazy- I had to tell him to turn down volume.. Ha! it was projector speaker causing too much ruckus- always a good sign!

So grateful this is user-friendly and end results really exceed expectations. I do recommend getting a specified bag/backpack to house, transport and Store projector in. Protect your investment and keep contained! Hoping info can somewhat help your decision in a layman sort of way- stay safe.
text_fidelity_b: Emotn C1 Mini WiFi Projector, 1080P Supported Portable Projector, 8500Lux Bluetooth 5.1 200" Movie Projector with HiFi Speaker, 50000H Lamp Life, Compatible with Smartphone/TV Stick/HDMI/USB/VGA/PS4
